changelog: v3.21.0's drawing tools were shipped without browser verification and were not usable. This release was built and verified against the real, unmodified project JS in an actual headless browser (Playwright + Chrome for Testing, driving js/chart.js + js/backtest.js + js/backtest-drawings.js through a mocked backend) -- every fix below was reproduced before the change and confirmed after it, not inferred from reading the code. What follows is what was actually observed, not what the code was supposed to do.

1. Unresponsive dragging -- root cause was a race condition, not a tolerance value. btUpdateOverlayInteractivity() toggled the overlay canvas's CSS pointer-events between 'auto'/'none' based on the LAST mousemove's hit-test, and was verified to still read 'none' at the exact instant a real mousedown fired on a handle, so the click fell through to the chart underneath. Fixed architecturally: the overlay is now permanently pointer-events:none, and every mouse/keyboard listener moved to the chart wrapper itself with {capture:true}, deciding synchronously on each event whether to claim it (stopPropagation) or leave it alone for the chart's own pan/zoom. Verified: dragging an existing handle now updates the drawing's data on every single pointermove (not just on release), confirmed by reading the value back mid-drag.

2. Position tool producing entry===take_profit / R:R 0.00 -- two independent, compounding bugs, both found and fixed via the same browser harness. (a) A real drag is mostly vertical (setting price levels is the point; the horizontal span is incidental), which collapsed both anchor points to the same time and gave the drawn box zero pixel width -- permanently unhittable after placement, which is what 'many clicks and drags needed' actually was. Fixed by giving the position tool a fixed 20-bar horizontal span at save time, independent of how far sideways the drag happened to go, applied identically to the live preview so what's shown while dragging matches what gets saved. (b) Magnet snapping had no price-distance cutoff: once a candle was chosen by time, the cursor's raw price always snapped to whichever of that candle's 4 OHLC values was nearest, no matter how far away the cursor actually was -- and because time-snapping depends only on x, a single vertical drag can only ever land on one candle, so entry and stop could silently collapse onto the exact same wick value. This is very likely the actual mechanism behind the entry===take_profit report. Fixed with a pixel-distance cutoff (10px): a price only snaps when the cursor is genuinely close to a wick on screen, otherwise the raw price is used. Verified: entry and stop are now distinct after a purely-vertical drag, R:R updates live during the drag, and the 3:1 lock correctly repositions the take-profit when the stop is dragged (checked against entry + risk*ratio by hand, both directions).

3. Long/short and the order button -- verified directly rather than assumed from the existing two-button code. Placing a Short draws stop above entry (risk) and take-profit below entry (reward), confirmed both directions' math against btComputeTpFromRatio's own sign. The tool's button reads 'Place Long' (green) or 'Place Short' (red) per tool, and clicking it was confirmed to submit to backtest_place_order with the exact direction ('Long'/'Short') and the drawing's own stop-loss/take-profit levels -- verified by inspecting the actual submitted payload.

4. Fibonacci labels -- 'Fib shows no level labels' was traced to a real bug, not a missing render call: fillText was firing correctly for every level on every frame, but extend_right (on by default) makes the line's own right edge equal to the overlay canvas's full pixel width, and the label was anchored 4px PAST that width -- outside the canvas's own clip region and therefore completely invisible regardless of colour or font. Fixed: labels are now right-aligned (per the ticket, matching TradingView's own convention) and anchored a small margin inside the canvas's actual edge, so they stay on-screen whether or not the line is extended. Verified in-browser that every enabled level renders its ratio and price, right-aligned, at an on-canvas coordinate, and that only 0/0.382/0.5/0.618/0.786/1 are enabled by default.

5. Toolbar icons -- the emoji/text placeholders (including the literal 'Fib' label) are replaced with a hand-authored, original line-icon set (24x24 viewBox, consistent 2px round-cap strokes) matching the visual weight of a Lucide/Tabler-style toolbar without tracing either library's or TradingView's own artwork. Verified rendered size is consistent (18x18) across all nine toolbar buttons and that hover/active state classes still toggle correctly; tooltips are native title attributes, unchanged from v3.21.0.

6. Verified in-browser, per the ticket's own checklist, for all four tools (position, fib, trend line, horizontal line/ray): place, drag each handle, drag the whole object, open the settings popover, delete. All passed. Also verified a placed drawing's on-screen position recomputes correctly (matching the chart's own coordinate APIs) after a pan, a zoom, and a full candle-array replacement -- the same operation js/backtest.js performs on every timeframe switch and replay step -- confirming the time/price anchoring design from v3.21.0 holds in practice, not just on paper.

Not re-litigated: the v3.21.0 architecture decision (canvas overlay anchored to real time/price rather than Lightweight Charts' logical index) was confirmed sound by this release's own testing and is unchanged.
release_notes: No schema changes in this release -- nothing to migrate. Per instruction, nothing was deployed as part of this turn.
